comments.comment: So? They are preventing kids from suffering and not living a normal life.

People with Down’s syndrome are beautiful, kind, amazing people — however, as wonderful as it can be for many people, having a child with Downs can be extremely difficult to manage, and extremely expensive, and it isn’t feasible for most families. Yes, adoption is an option, but the reality is that most disabled children who are put up for adoption are never adopted, and do not live lives where they are given the love and support they need. But this is all irrelevant, because these statistics are not from mid to late term abortions, meaning that it’s not even a baby yet. A woman should have the right to choose whether or not she should have to bring a child into this world, and it’s not our place to judge what factors went into her decision making.
